recipes.name: Run 1
dims: Wedge (1/8 of a log), from a 12 in log
Length along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face
Length along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the flat side

steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 9.70 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the flat side on the saw table, with the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the flat side against the fence, the keeper to the RIGHT of the blade. Mitre 0° (square across). Bevel 9.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, left of the blade, is a tapered piece: 1.14 in along the point, down to 0.50 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Cut 2 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the slanted sawn face on the saw table, with the bark corner of the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the RIGHT of the blade. Mitre 52.0° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the RIGHT. Bevel 25.7° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Measure from the first cut and mark: 8.31 in along the point; 0.00 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the flat side; 4.49 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the slanted sawn face -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, left of the blade, is only a sliver. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Cut 3 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the slanted sawn face on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 38.1° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 45.2° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Measure from the first cut and mark: 8.31 in along the point; 0.00 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the flat side; 4.49 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the slanted sawn face -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 70.86 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the flat side, down to 62.55 in along the point -- keep it: it is long enough for a shorter piece. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 8.31 in along the point, 4.49 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face, 0.00 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the flat side. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as run 1: on a sawn face against the flat side, point toward the open run (like the frame).

steps.title: Split the log in eighths
steps.text: Buck the 12 in log to the strut length. Halve it through the pith with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf), quarter each half, then halve each quarter: eight wedges, each with two sawn faces 6.00 in wide meeting at the pith, bark 4.59 in across.
